## Goal

Make the administration area safe to expose: a verified owner account must exist before anything is reachable, and that must keep holding while the application runs.

## Context

Any authenticated user of the administration collection has full rights over the whole admin area, including customer and accounting records. After the documented initialisation the administrator table is empty, and the framework offers its own first-user registration. The deployment procedure does not yet make an existing, verified administrator a precondition for serving public traffic. Details are in the owner's private tracker. The second factor is a separate package (SC-026) because it needs its own decision, implementation and acceptance.

## Scope

- Refuse to serve production traffic while no verified administrator exists. This has to hold at boot **and** at request time: a deployment that starts with an administrator must also refuse once the last one is removed, or when the database it talks to changes underneath it. Cache the answer only in a way that a change invalidates within seconds, and state the chosen window in the PR.
- The same condition covers a fresh install, a restore from backup and the state after the last administrator is removed.
- A private initialisation step in `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` for creating the owner account before the site is reachable, with exact commands.
- A comparison of the two ways to add a second factor, in the application or at an identity gateway in front of it, written as decision D-013 for the owner: what each protects, what it costs, whether it is a paid service, what happens if the owner loses the factor, and what it means for the admin API routes and not only the panel. Recommend one. Do not implement it here.
- `docs/LAUNCH-CHECKLIST.md` updated, with the second factor listed as its own item (SC-026).

## Out of scope

- Implementing the second factor (SC-026).
- Changing customer authentication (SC-021).
- Changing access rules of collections beyond what this needs.
- Signing up for any paid service.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A fresh install refuses production traffic until an administrator exists, proven by a test.
- [ ] Removing the last administrator while the application is running makes it refuse again within the stated window, proven by a test, not by reasoning.
- [ ] Development mode stays usable and the existing suites pass.
- [ ] The owner-account procedure has been followed once end to end and the output is recorded on the issue.
- [ ] D-013 is written with a recommendation.
- [ ] Independent review approves.

## Required tests

- Unit and integration tests for the boot condition and for the request-time condition.
- A manual run of the initialisation procedure, recorded on the issue.
- All standard checks.

## Dependencies

- SC-003
